results.title: Installer helper crashes on 32-bit phones with older kernels
results.section: Installer helper crashes on 32-bit phones with older kernels
results.text:
On some 32-bit (armv7 / armv8l) phones whose kernel is older than 5.1, the `andronix` helper inside the distro can crash at start with a `futexwakeup ... returned -38` and `SIGSEGV` message. A fix is coming in the next installer release.

The crash usually does not stop the install itself. Let the install finish before you start the desktop:

1. Wait until the install screen says the install is done. Don't run `andronix desktop` while packages are still downloading.
2. If the install was interrupted, start it again from the app.
3. If it still fails, send a problem report from the app so we can check the log.

results.title: Requirements
results.text:
On a phone with Android 7 or without a 64-bit ARM processor (x86, or 32-bit ARM), Andronix runs Linux inside Termux instead. What those phones need: [Requirements for Termux](/termux/requirements).

Install in the app:

results.title: Requirements for Termux
results.text: Most phones are **arm64**, and every distro supports it. Some distros also run on 32-bit arm, x86 and x86_64 devices (like Chromebooks); see [Supported distros](/reference/distros). You don't need to check this yourself: the installer checks your CPU first and tells you if a distro doesn't support it.

results.title: Install Apps
results.text:
| Distro | Command |
|---|---|
| Debian, Kali Linux | `sudo apt install chromium` |
| Fedora | `sudo dnf install chromium` |
| Arch, Manjaro | `sudo pacman -S chromium` |
| Alpine | `sudo apk add chromium` |
| Void Linux | Not packaged for Void. |

Chromium can't use its sandbox in Andronix. If it doesn't open from the app menu, start it from a terminal with:

```bash copy
chromium --no-sandbox
```

On 32-bit (armv7) phones, browsers may fail to start.

results.title: Requirements for Termux
results.text:
This page is for Andronix with Termux, on phones that can't run Linux in the app (Android 7, or no 64-bit ARM processor). For everything else, see [Requirements](/start-here/requirements).

In Termux, Andronix runs on more devices than in the app, including Android 7, 32-bit ARM, x86 and x86_64:

| | Command line only | With a desktop |
|---|---|---|
| **Android** | 7 or newer | 7 or newer |
| **CPU** | arm64 (most phones), also arm, x86 and x86_64 for some distros | Same |
| **Free storage** | about 0.5 GB | 1.5 to 2 GB (about 3 GB for KDE Plasma) |
| **RAM** | 2 GB | 3 GB or more is comfortable; 4 GB or more for KDE Plasma |
| **Root** | Not needed | Not needed |

results.title: Installing Modded OS
results.text:
- **Sign in** to the Andronix app. Your purchases are linked to your account.
- **A 64-bit phone:** Modded OS isn't available on 32-bit phones; the app tells you if yours is one.
- **One install per distro:** a Modded edition is installed into the folder of the distro it's built on, so it can't sit next to the free distro of the same base, or another edition built on it. For example, Modded 2.0 Ubuntu KDE replaces the free Ubuntu. If one is already there, the install stops and tells you; to replace it, add `--reinstall` to the command. It asks before deleting anything, so [back up](/use/backups) what you want to keep first.
- **Download limits:** each account can download a Modded OS a set number of times per day and per month. Most people never reach the limit, and Premium raises it. If you need more for a good reason, [contact us](mailto:support@andronix.app).
